brief: Meta's Muse consumer AI agent, launched 8 September, hit 2.5 million downloads in 13 days, outpacing ChatGPT's comparable launch window per Apptopia (1.8 million vs 1.3 million US/Canada iOS downloads), and tech and Asian AI supply-chain shares rallied on the news. UBS calls this early evidence that consumer AI agents can reach broad adoption. Agents could add a third monetization channel, transactions such as purchases, travel booking, and bill payment, beyond existing subscriptions and advertising. Wider adoption should let monetization catch up with hyperscalers' AI infrastructure spending, though application-layer leadership stays fluid as platforms compete on distribution and data. Because agents are more CPU-intensive than chatbots, stronger adoption should lift demand across processors, memory, packaging, servers, networking, power, and cooling, though UBS prefers diversified exposure over a single semiconductor trade. UBS stays constructive on the AI trade overall. Separately, UBS flags three items. The Trump-Xi summit (23-25 September) may extend the trade truce and ease near-term uncertainty without a fundamental reset. Roche's Phase II obesity drug cut body weight 15.5% on average after 48 weeks at the highest dose. Copper trades near record highs on tight supply and Chinese demand, and UBS views near-term weakness as a buying opportunity.
